subject: Cannot configure shiny server on ec2 machine

messages.author: 4466c992e65f1ad8
messages.subject: Cannot configure shiny server on ec2 machine
parts:
I am trying to follow the instructions here on starting and stopping shiny server

http://rstudio.github.io/shiny-server/latest/#stopping-and-starting

I installed shiny-server on an ec2 linux machine which I found to be based off centos.  I followed the directions here which install using an RPM instead of the old node js and npm way

http://www.rstudio.com/shiny/server/install-opensource

My installation was put in /srv/shiny-server.  The first thing I noticed was that I could not get shiny to start by running

start shiny-server
bash: start: command not found

However, I could get it to start by running /srv/shiny-server/bin/shiny-server.  So naturally I just added /srv/shiny-server/bin to my PATH variable.

Running shiny has been fine so far, but I've run into an error on my shiny app and need to restart the service.  I tried to run this command

/sbin/service shiny-server stop

but now I receive this error

which: no shiny-server in (/sbin:/usr/sbin:/bin:/usr/bin)
Stopping shiny-server: not running.                        [FAILED]

Given that this is the second time shiny could not be found I feel like my installation was incorrect.  Any tips on how to debug this?  Any tips on how to find and kill the process so I can just run /opt/shiny-server/bin/shiny-server?

--
Jeffrey Wong
My portfolio: http://jeffreyctwong.com

messages.author: 3da48b33a2f506a9
messages.subject: Re: Cannot configure shiny server on ec2 machine
parts:
Hi Jeffrey,

Can you tell from the rpm what version of Shiny Server you have installed? Or could you run this command: 

shiny-server --version

I am surprised that you have installation in /srv/shiny-server; the install location should be /opt/shiny-server. My suggestion is that you remove your installation, make sure your file system is clean, and then install the rpm again.

And based on what you said, it seems that you are running on CentOS 5. (You can verify that by running this command: "cat /etc/issue")
If the installation happens correctly, server will start automatically. You can verify that by pointing your browser to http://localhost:3838

And you should be able to use the following command to start (or stop) the server as needed:

sudo /sbin/service shiny-server start

The location of log file is: /var/log/shiny-server.log  please check the file for any errors if your server hasn't started properly.

Hope this helps, and let us if you still have issues.
Fereshteh

messages.author: 4466c992e65f1ad8
messages.subject: Re: Cannot configure shiny server on ec2 machine
parts:
Solved the problem!  The issue was that the installation needed to run under sudo.  I was logged in as root and just ran a plain command

yum install --nogpgcheck shiny-server-0.4.0.15-x86_64.rpm -y

which gave the error below. The strange issue is that the user 'root' did not show up inside visudo, so it reported that I was not a sudoer and didn't truly complete the install. After I added myself to visudo and reran the install everything worked. Maybe this edge case could be added where if sudo privileges are not available the install should not report Complete!

  Installing     : shiny-server                                                                                                                                                                                                         1/1
